ai.description: *Rhabdops aquaticus* is a slender snake reaching 60–80 cm. It is dark brown or black above with a white belly and possesses a distinctively blunt snout and small, dark eyes. It is strictly aquatic.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhabdops aquaticus* is best distinguished by its lack of a loreal scale, causing the prefrontal scales to contact the upper labials directly.
ai.habitat: *Rhabdops aquaticus* inhabits clear, rocky streams within evergreen forests and high-altitude grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations above 800 meters.
ai.behavior: *Rhabdops aquaticus* is a nocturnal snake that primarily hunts for fish and amphibians by actively foraging in shallow, flowing streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhabdops aquaticus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Rhabdops aquaticus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka at elevations between 400 and 1,200m.
